frameworks.name: EU AI Act (benchmark)
frameworks.role: Legal checklist for high-risk AI systems, used as a yardstick: the system is operated in Pakistan, so the Act does not apply by law.
frameworks.how: Each article is the acceptance condition of the controls tagged with it. The technical file is produced from the same records (Annex IV style). Status is met when every tagged control is met.

frameworks.name: NIST AI RMF 1.0
frameworks.role: Voluntary framework; the working loop of the management system.
frameworks.how: Read the control register by function. The status per function is the current profile; the target profile is every function met. No certificate exists.

requirements.title: Context, intended use, risks and impacts
Treat risks, respond to incidents, monitor and improve

frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 42001 (with 23894 and 42005)
frameworks.role: Certifiable AI management system; here an internal audit against it, no certification sought.
frameworks.how: Clauses 4 to 10 are the governance layer; the Annex A areas are carried by the controls tagged with them. This register is the statement of applicability.

requirements.title: Operation: impact assessment and life cycle

frameworks.name: OECD AI Principles
frameworks.role: Values the system is checked against; the OECD classification framework profiles the system once (governance/impact_assessment.md).
frameworks.how: Each principle points at the controls that put it into practice.

requirements.title: Inclusive growth, sustainable development and well-being
Human rights and democratic values, fairness and privacy

frameworks.name: Data governance (DAMA-DMBOK, OCHA Data Responsibility)
frameworks.role: Practice for the training data and the uploaded imagery.
frameworks.how: DAMA knowledge areas and the OCHA data-responsibility guidance as a checklist for the data controls.

requirements.title: Humanitarian data responsibility: minimum data, known recipients

frameworks.name: Pakistan (legal setting)
frameworks.role: The laws and policy where the system is used. Status of the data protection bill to be checked against the official text before citing.
frameworks.how: Applies to image intake (rights, privacy), access and security, and the responsible-AI commitments of the national policy.

requirements.title: Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016 (unauthorised access, data security)
National AI Policy 2025: responsible, human-overseen AI
